PMET Resources Inc. (the "Company" or "PMET")

) (OTCQX: PMETF) (FSE: R9GA) is pleased to announce the results of its Updated CV5 Feasibility Study ("Updated FS") at the Company's wholly owned Shaakichiuwaanaan Property (the "Property" or "Project") located in the Eeyou Istchee James Bay region of Quebec, Canada.

The Updated FS is underpinned by a Mineral Reserve derived from the CV5 Pegmatite's Indicated Mineral Resource component, part of the current Shaakichiuwaanaan Consolidated Mineral Resource Estimate ("MRE"), which is one of the top 10 largest known lithium pegmatite MREs globally (see news release dated

While a final investment decision ("FID") has yet to be made for the Shaakichiuwaanaan Project, the Updated FS reaffirms the CV5 Pegmatite's potential to position the Company as a globally significant spodumene concentrate producer and it firmly demonstrates its potential to become a top-tier tantalum concentrate producer.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
SCOPE

The Updated FS outlines an improved development scenario for the Project inclusive of lithium and tantalum production at CV5, working within the constraints of the scope established under the Company's existing Environmental and Social Impact Assessment ("ESIA"). Building on the Company's 2025 Lithium-Only Feasibility Study on CV5, it retains the hybrid underground ("UG") and open-pit ("OP") mining model while incorporating production of tantalum alongside that of lithium to maximise the value of the Mineral Resource.

The ESIA filed in March 2026 established the broad development scope for which final mine authorisation is being sought, including processing capacity of up to 5.1 Mtpa. The Updated FS now optimises the phased development case within this existing ESIA authorisation framework, accessing and leveraging the high-grade UG Nova Zone earlier. This improves early years cashflow generation while preserving optionality and flexibility over time to unlock the full potential of the Shaakichiuwaanaan Project and potentially position it as a leading, low-cost lithium and tantalum raw materials supplier to North American, European, and Asian markets.
CONTRIBUTING SPECIALIST CONSULTANTS/ADVISORS

The Company engaged external consultant, BBA Consultants, as lead consultant, with contributions from Primero Group Americas Inc., AtkinsRéalis Group Inc., Vision Geochemistry Ltd., Alius Mine Consulting, WSP Canada Inc., Mailloux Hydrogéologie, and CGM Expert, to prepare an independent Updated Feasibility Study and Technical Report for the CV5 Pegmatite (lithium-tantalum) at the Shaakichiuwaanaan Project.
STUDY OUTCOMES

The Updated FS reaffirms that the CV5 Pegmatite, with a nameplate design production rate of up to 800,000 tonnes per annum of SC5.5 spodumene concentrate, positioning PMET as a globally significant spodumene concentrate producer. With planned ore processing capacity of up to 5.1 Mtpa and production spanning approximately 20 years, the Project is set to become a large-scale, long-life lithium pegmatite operation. Further, the Updated FS establishes the potential for PMET to produce tantalum as a valuable co-product to the lithium operation and therefore also become a globally significant tantalum producer.

Through the application of the tantalum revenue as a credit to its spodumene concentrate production, Shaakichiuwaanaan materially improves on its overall competitive cost position, with a projected LOM AISC (FOB Quebec ports)8 of ~CA$657/t net of tantalum credit (~US$480/t net of tantalum credit). This improved cost profile, alongside exposure to a second commodity, underscores the Project's overall resilience to challenging market conditions, but also the ability to deliver substantial returns and potential upside from improved pricing and stronger market conditions.

The Updated FS delivers an after-tax NPV8% of ~CA$5,100M (~US$3,723M) at an assumed long-term spodumene concentrate price of US$1,788/t (SC5.5, FOB Quebec ports) and long-term tantalite concentrate price of US$120/lb of contained Ta2O5 (20% Ta2O5 basis), Table 1. This represents a significant improvement over the previously published FS (see news release dated October 20, 2025), owing for the most part to a combination of revenue addition from tantalum, improved lithium pricing assumptions, and broader Project refinements. Total development capital of ~CA$2,063M (or ~CA$1,675M, net of anticipated pre-production credit and tax credits) is consistent with the overall scale of the Project. The Updated FS estimate is inclusive of an 11% Project contingency.

Importantly, the Updated FS reaffirms that Shaakichiuwaanaan's CV5 is both technically feasible and economically viable and positions the Project to become a cornerstone supplier to the North American, European, and Asian critical minerals supply chains. The combination of scale, longevity, and cost competitiveness, together with the ability to supply a coarse, high-quality SC5.5 spodumene concentrate from a DMS only operation alongside a 20% Ta2O5 secondary tantalite concentrate, provides a strong platform for future growth.

On a like-for-like basis removing impact of lithium price and exchange rate assumptions (using FS 2025 lithium price and exchange rate), the Updated FS increases after-tax NPV8% by CA$0.7 billion to CA$2.3 billion (with CA$180M contribution from mining plan improvements and CA$519M from tantalum co-product addition) and after-tax IRR increases from 18.1% to 24.6%. AISC would see a significant reduction, from CA$800/t (US$597/t) to CA$657/t (US$490).

NEXT STEPS

The Company will continue to advance detailed engineering for the Phase 1 development. In parallel, the Company is advancing a PEA-level of assessment on an alternate development scenario inclusive of both CV5 and the Company's higher grade CV13 pegmatite for lithium, caesium, and tantalum.

To support this optimisation process and further de-risk the Project, the Company continues to advance its UG bulk sample program targeting the CV5 high-grade Nova Zone, which will provide additional data to validate key design assumptions, test product specification and quality at scale, and confirm mine plan enhancements.

In parallel, the completion of the Updated FS positions the Company to further advance its ongoing discussions with customers, strategic investors and government stakeholders, reflecting the Shaakichiuwaanaan Project's importance to develop a robust western-facing critical minerals supply chain.

The FID remains targeted for late 2027, subject to securing project approvals and funding. It will take into account detailed engineering, prevailing market conditions, and the Company's commercial relationships and customer requirements across the critical minerals supply chain.
FEASIBILITY STUDY - DISCUSSION
Project Location

The Shaakichiuwaanaan Property is located in the Eeyou Istchee James Bay region of Québec, Canada, approximately 220 km east of Radisson, Québec, and 240 km north-northeast of Nemaska, Québec. The Property consists of two (2) primary EER11 groups, one straddling KM-270 of the Trans-Taiga Road and the other with its northern border located directly south of KM-270, approximately 6 km from the Trans-Taiga Road and powerline infrastructure corridor (Figure 1).

The La Grande 4 ("LG-4") hydroelectric dam complex is located approximately 30 km north-northeast of the Property. The CV5 LCT Pegmatite is located central to the Property, approximately 13 km south of KM-270 on the Trans-Taiga Road, 14 km south of the powerline, and approximately 50 km southwest of the LG-4 dam complex.

The Property is situated on Category III Land within the Eeyou Istchee James Bay Territory (Cree Nation of Chisasibi, and Cree Nation of Mistissini), as defined under the James Bay and Northern Québec Agreement ("JBNQA"). The Eeyou Istchee James Bay Regional Government is the designated municipality for the region including the Property.

The CV5 Pegmatite is a Li-Cs-Ta (LCT) pegmatite situated central to the Property within the Guyer Greenstone Belt, considered part of the larger La Grande River Greenstone Belt, and intrudes predominantly amphibolite, metasediment, and lesser ultramafic rock types. The principal lithium mineral is spodumene which is present typically as decimetre to metre scale crystals. The principal tantalum mineral is tantalite (±columbite).

The CV5 Pegmatite, including the principal dyke, is modelled to extend continuously over a lateral distance of at least 5.0 km and remains open along strike at both ends and to depth along a large portion of its length (Figure 2). The principal dyke, comprising approximately 76% of total CV5 resource tonnage, ranges from <10 m to more than 125 m in true width, and may pinch and swell aggressively along strike, as well as up and down dip. It is primarily the thickest at near-surface to moderate depths (<225 m), forming a relatively bulbous, elongated shape, which may flare to surface and to depth variably along its length. The principal dyke also hosts the high-grade Nova Zone, which has been traced over a strike length of approximately 1.5 km and includes multiple drill intersections ranging from 2 m to 25 m (core length) at >5% Li2O, within a significantly wider mineralized zone of >2% Li2O.

The mine design and Mineral Reserve Estimate for the CV5 LCT pegmatite were completed to a level appropriate for feasibility studies. The Mineral Reserves were estimated in accordance with the CIM Estimation of Mineral Resources & Mineral Reserves Best Practice Guidelines (November 29, 2019) and CIM Definition Standards for Mineral Resources and Reserves (May 10, 2014) and also comply with the JORC Code 2012.

In line with these standards, the Mineral Reserves for the CV5 LCT Pegmatite are based solely on Indicated Mineral Resources, and for lithium and tantalum only. Any Inferred Mineral Resources that fall within the mine design envelope have been treated as waste and assigned a grade of 0.0% Li2O for the purposes of mine planning and economic evaluation.

To evaluate the potentially economical portion of the Mineral Resource Estimate, separate break-even COGs were calculated for the OP and the UG components. The calculation used OPEX reflecting current labour and fuel price, inclusive of mining, processing, G&A, concentrate transport, and royalties. The metallurgical recovery assumption followed a grade/recovery curve determined via extensive testing undertaken by SGS Canada. The COG calculations also take into account dilution and mining recovery assumptions. The resulting COGs used for the OP and the UG Mineral Reserves are 0.40% and 0.70% Li2O respectively. The revenue factor for the COG calculation was based solely on lithium, with no value derived from tantalum content for COG calculations purposes.

A zone-by-zone approach was applied to validate the economic viability of each area of the deposit by integrating zone-specific sustaining capital costs into the economic analysis for the UG Reserve, whereby stope clusters that did not support development costs to access them, were not converted to Reserves. The UG stopes located within the crown pillar (0-85m from lake bottom) were not converted to Reserves.

Environmental and social baseline studies and an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) have been submitted to federal and provincial regulators and the permitting process is ongoing. The Project is located on EERs held by the Company within Québec, Canada. No material tenure issues have been identified. Infrastructure assumptions include connection to Hydro-Québec's power network via a proposed 120 kV transmission line, year-round access via the Trans-Taiga Road, concentrate haulage by road to Matagami and onward rail transport to Québec port facilities. Transport, water management, waste management, tailings storage and closure requirements have been incorporated into the feasibility study design and economic evaluation. The Company continues engagement with Eeyou/Cree stakeholders and an Impact Benefit Agreement is expected prior to operations. No material legal, environmental, permitting or governmental impediments have been identified that would prevent development of the Project, although final approvals remain outstanding. No additional assumptions have been applied to the Mineral Reserve Estimate for the purposes of these factors. Mineral Reserves are included in the Mineral Resource for the CV5 Pegmatite.

It is the opinion of the Qualified/Competent Person that the Mineral Reserve Estimate is supported by appropriate design, scheduling and costing work reported to a feasibility study level of detail. Sufficient modifying factors and economic considerations have been applied to the Indicated Mineral Resource to declare the Probable Mineral Reserve. As such, Mineral Reserves are reported commensurate with the Probable classification.

Mining and Production Summary

The CV5 LCT Pegmatite deposit consists of a large principal dyke, flanked by several smaller dykes striking approximately east-west. Planned mining operations will incorporate both mechanized long hole open stoping underground ("UG") mining and conventional open-pit ("OP") mining methods. The pegmatite dykes dip at approximately 70-80° northerly and extend over a strike length of approximately 5.0 km with mineralization intersected as deep as 450 m vertical depth from surface. A significant portion of the orebody is located under Lake 001, which will require partial dewatering to enable the full-scale Phase 2 OP operations.
The Project follows a staged two-phase execution strategy:
Phase 1

prioritizes high-grade underground Nova Zone ore to feed a 2.2 Mtpa capacity dense media separation ("DMS") concentration plant. During Year 1, UG production is supplemented by a small Starter Pit requiring minimal pre-stripping and involving no lake disturbance to sustain the processing plant. The UG production is sufficient to sustain planned processing capacity starting in Year 2 resulting in the Starter Pit operations being idled after Year 1.
Phase 2

Expansion involves construction of a second DMS concentration plant starting in Year 3 with commissioning in Year 4, adding a further 2.9 Mtpa of processing capacity and supplied with ore coming from resumption of OP operations at full scale. Thereafter, UG and OP production will be coordinated to maximize utilization and recovery of both plants over the near 20 year mine life, with a total installed processing capacity of 5.1 Mtpa of ore.

Mining Methods and AssumptionsUnderground Mine

The UG operation comprises a single ramp accessible through a portal located near the run-of-mine ("ROM") pad. The selected mining method is long-hole open stoping ("LHOS") with cemented paste backfill ("CPB"), using both transverse (96% of stopes) and longitudinal (4% of stopes) stoping techniques (Figure 11).

The LOM for the UG mine is expected to be 21 years including construction, development, pre-production, and the full production period. Over this LOM, the UG mine is expected to be at full production for 15 years, with production declining in the last three years. At full production, the UG mine is expected to achieve a production rate of approximately 5,700 tpd of ore, with 5,375 tpd from stope production and an average 325 tpd from lateral development. Development of the UG mine includes approximately 81.1 km of lateral and 1.3 km of vertical development to be excavated. A total of 34.9 Mt of ore is expected to be mined at an average diluted grade of 1.51% Li2O and 172 ppm Ta2O5. The primary production and development equipment fleet includes 18 t battery electric vehicle (BEV) load-haul-dump (LHD), coupled with 50 tonnes BEV-powered underground mining trucks. The UG mine is planned to be owner-operated throughout the LOM, with the exception of the first three years of development, which is planned to be contracted out.
Open-Pit Mine
The OP operation will take place over two distinct time horizons and with two distinct scopes:

Starter Pit: Mining will commence with a very small Starter Pit requiring minimal pre-stripping and no impact to the nearby lake. The Starter Pit will be located within the main pit footprint, maintaining a 60 m stand-off distance to Lake 001. Its production (less than 700 kt) is only meant to supplement the ramp-up of UG operations in order to sustain the processing plant in the first year of operation. After Year 1, OP mining operations at the Starter Pit will be idled;

Main OP operations: Upon launching the Phase 2 Expansion, mining of the OP will resume, albeit at a much larger rate and scale and ramp up total ore production from the Project to its 5.1 Mtpa nameplate capacity.

The main OP operation will utilize a fleet of diesel-powered equipment, including drills, hydraulic shovels and excavators, and off-highway haul trucks. The OP peak mining rate is 23.0 Mtpa over the LOM. A total of 48.2 Mt at 1.10% Li2O and 132ppm Ta2O5 of ore will come from the OP. A total of 215.9 Mt of material, including ore, waste rock, and overburden, will be moved during the LOM, resulting in an average stripping ratio of 3.5.

The primary loading and hauling fleet will consist of 15 m3 diesel-hydraulic shovels for waste and 7 m3 diesel-hydraulic excavators for ore paired with 140 t off-highway mining trucks. While the main OP operations will be owner-operated, the Starter Pit is assumed to be operated with smaller equipment and contracted out.

Processing Summary

The mineral processing facility is designed to produce both spodumene (5.5% Li2O and <2.0% Fe2O3) and tantalite (20% Ta2O3) concentrates from the run-of-mine (ROM – ore mined and delivered to stockpile). The facility will include ROM stockpiling, crushing, beneficiation, pastefill preparation, pastefill mixing and pumping and tailings dewatering with handling.

The Updated Feasibility process plant design and production outcomes have been informed by multiple extensive bench and pilot scale testwork programs. Further, samples contributing to those programs are derived from a wide-spread and representative data-set, to inform a feasibility level assessment.

The Project will have two process trains (referred to as DMS1 associated with Phase 1 and DMS2 associated with Phase 2). Operations begin with only DMS1, processing 2.2 Mtpa of high-grade ore predominantly from UG mining, supplemented in Year 1 by a small "starter" OP (referred as the Starter Pit) while UG production is ramping up. In Year 4 of the mine life, DMS2 becomes operational, with both trains operating in parallel for the rest of the LOM. Phase 2 processes lower-grade OP ore at 2.9 Mtpa. The total installed processing capacity once DMS2 is online is 5.1 Mtpa across the whole facility.

DMS1 and DMS2 are mostly separate process trains. Although similar in design, the two crushing/processing plants are largely unique and operate independently. Interaction between the two plants occurs for the spodumene concentrate storage, the pastefill preparation circuit, the final tantalite concentration stage, and for the tailings dewatering and handling. Figure 15 presents a simplified process flow diagram.

Each process train will be inside three (3) main buildings: the primary crushing building, the secondary and tertiary crushing building, and the main processing plant. The crushed mineralized material will be stored in silos. The mineral processing facility is designed to produce spodumene concentrate at 5.5% Li2O (Figure 15) and tantalite concentrate at 20% Ta2O5.
The following are the major process circuit descriptions:

Crushing circuit: Receives and reduces the ROM material to a product with a top size of 9.5 mm. The crushing circuit has three stages and is closed with screens. The crushed product reports to a fine ore silo which feeds the processing plant;

Spodumene processing: Plant feed is screened into three size fractions; coarse, fine, and ultrafine, with material smaller than 0.65 mm (DMS bypass fraction) reporting directly to pastefill preparation, which will feed the tantalum processing circuit. Each size fraction reports to a dedicated DMS circuit where there is a separation of material based on particle density. The fine and ultrafine concentrates are further processed via magnetic separation to both lessen the elemental iron that reports to the final concentrate and to recover tantalum-bearing minerals for further processing in the tantalum recovery circuit;

Tantalite processing: Tantalum is recovered from non-spodumene concentrate process streams (i.e., spodumene processing tailings/waste streams; DMS bypass, DMS magnetics, and DMS floats that are made available during pastefill preparation (i.e. middlings). A primary concentrate (<3% Ta2O5) is generated via conventional gravity recovery and magnetic concentration and is subsequently upgraded to the target final concentrate grade of 20% Ta2O5 via shaking tables;

Pastefill Preparation/Pastefill: DMS floats (fine, ultrafine), DMS bypass (post tantalite recovery) and DMS magnetics (also post tantalite recovery) are fed to a closed ball mill circuit for grinding. The ground material is thickened and pumped to the paste backfill plant where the material is filtered, mixed with binder and water and then pumped to the target stopes underground.

Tailings dewatering/handling: The DMS rejects (i.e., floats) that are not being used as pastefill in the pastefill preparation circuit report to a conveyor belt where they are stacked in a pile outside prior to be transported to the tailings pile.

Concentrate Transport

The mine site is located along the Trans-Taiga Road, approximately 844 km from the Matagami Transshipment Center. This route includes 290 km on the east–west Trans-Taiga Road and 554 km on the north–south Billy Diamond Highway.

Transportation of spodumene concentrate to Matagami was modelled as a contracted service. At nominal plant capacity, daily output totals 2,302 t of spodumene concentrate to be hauled. Trucks with a 72 tonnes payload (including 5% moisture) are assumed for this study and will require special annual permits from the regulator including, but not limited to, approval from the Ministère des transports et de la mobilité durable ("MTMD"), the Ministère des ressources naturelles et des forêts ("MRNF"), and Société de développement de la Baie-James ("SDBJ").

These 72 t vehicles will consist of a four-axle tractor and a five-axle bi-train trailer, equipped with a trailer cover and side-discharge system. Accounting for an additional 5% capacity margin, approximately 32 truck trips will be required daily between the mine and Matagami from 2032 to 2048. Operations will run 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, year-round. A fleet of 80 trucks will be maintained to provide a 25% buffer for maintenance, road restrictions and/or environmental disruptions. Reduced payloads during spring thaw period have been factored into the estimates.

The Company recently signed a Letter of Intent ("LOI") with the City of Matagami for the planned transshipment of spodumene concentrate, transferring the spodumene concentrate inbound from the mining site via trucks to rail cars outbound to port at Matagami's transshipment yard (see news release dated October 4, 2026).

From Matagami, the Updated FS assumes transport of spodumene concentrate by train to a maritime terminal along the Saint-Lawrence river for vessel loading. Railcars will be 2,700 cu.ft. gondola cars and will carry 86 tonnes of concentrate each. A track loading restriction on the rail segment between Matagami and Lebel-sur-Quévillon limits the maximum gross railcar loads to 263,000 lb (119,300 kg) and this restriction governs railcar loading for the entire transportation corridor.

Annual shipments will total approximately 9,300 trips – which amounts to approximately 179 railcars per week required, assuming a 52-week operational year. A full round trip, including loading, CN transport, transit time, and unloading, is estimated at roughly 25 days. To sustain operations, approximately 700 leased railcars will be required at full-scale operations. For the Updated FS, an average price between the Montreal and Trois-Rivières port was assumed but all ports options were averaging similar prices and further analysis and negotiations will continue to secure final contracts in the next few months.  Therefore, the Updated FS uses the average pricing between Montréal and Trois-Rivières port options as all port options remain under consideration.
Logistics costs have increased within the Updated Feasibility Study as a function of;
General inflationary pressure;
Diesel fuel price and surcharge; and
Increase in scope (including but not limited to) slightly reduced truck and railcar capacity, seasonal haulage variation and loads, transhipment and port costs.

Transportation of the tantalite concentrate to market is modeled as an incremental cost to material transport to site, as the tantalite concentrate will be shipped in 1 tonne bulk bags as backhaul on standard 30 tonnes capacity flat bed trucks used to bring reagents and materials to site.
The Updated FS analysis provides a robust basis for the logistics strategy, and final routing will be confirmed through commercial negotiations with the entities involved.

The Company continues to advance the environmental assessment and permitting progress for the Shaakichiuwaanaan Project. The regulatory process reached a major milestone in March 2026, when the Company officially submitted the comprehensive Environmental and Social Impact Assessment ("ESIA") documentation to both federal and provincial regulators. The Impact Assessment Agency of Canada ("IAAC") subsequently deemed the federal ESIA submission complete, launching the first statutory public consultation period in April 2026. The submission built upon over three years of environmental baseline data collection and continuous community consultations.

Additionally, in accordance with Section 22 of the James Bay and Northern Quebec Agreement ("JBNQA"), the Project is reviewed by a series of committees made up of Eeyou/Cree and Provincial representatives. In 2024, the Project Notice was evaluated by the Evaluating Committee (COMEV), which provided recommendations concerning the scope of the provincial assessment. Following the March 2026 submission, the ESIA is now subject to examination by the Review Committee (COMEX), which will provide recommendations to the Provincial Administrator regarding project authorization and any associated conditions. A final mine authorization decision from the Provincial Administrator (the Deputy-Minister at Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Protection de la biodiversité, de la Faune et des Parcs, MELCCFP) is projected within 18 to 24 months from the official filing (per PMET Resources Shaakichiuwaanaan ESIA submission of March 2026).

The Updated Feasibility Study incorporates refinements to the Project design while maintaining alignment with the submitted scope of the ongoing environmental assessments. The Company continues to regularly engage with the Cree Nation of Chisasibi, the Eeyou/Cree Nation Government, affected Eeyou/Cree communities and regulatory authorities to support the assessment process, address environmental and social considerations, and advance the Project toward the required mine authorisations.
Full closure and reclamation considerations have been included within the Updated FS outcomes.
Exploration

Widely recognized as a Tier-1 pegmatite critical mineral asset globally, hosting one the world's largest lithium-tantalum pegmatites as well as the world's largest caesium (pollucite) pegmatite, Shaakichiuwaanaan continues to hold considerable exploration upside.

To date, eleven (11) distinct LCT pegmatite clusters have been discovered at the Property with Mineral Resources determined for three (3) – CV5, CV13, and CV4 (Figure 16). A total of five (5) clusters remain to be drill tested and outline a prospective trend exceeding 10 km in length (the "Mickel Trend"). Significant potential is present to grow Mineral Resources through further step-out drill delineation of the CV5, CV13, and CV4 pegmatites – which all remain open in several directions – drill testing along the Mickel Trend, as well as other prospective areas of the Property that remain to be evaluated.

Additionally, the current Mineral Reserve includes only the CV5 Pegmatite and is derived solely from the CV5 Pegmatite's Indicated Mineral Resource. The CV13 and CV4 pegmatite Mineral Resources, including the high-grade Vega Zone within CV13, are not included in the current Mineral Reserve.
Government Tax Incentive/Assistance
The Company, in consultation with its tax advisors, reviewed the Project's initial capital budget and has updated its assessment of eligible Project expenditures and associated tax benefits.

The CTM-ITC provides up to a 30% refundable tax credit on eligible capital costs for mining companies engaged in critical mineral extraction and processing activities. Based on the review, the Company and its tax advisors estimate that up to CA$880M of expected costs associated with the Project may be deemed eligible for the CTM-ITC, leading to a potential refundable investment tax credit of approximately CA$214M. In addition, Québec's tax holiday for large investment projects could generate approximately CA$197 million in income tax savings, while the Tax Credit Relating to Resources (TCRR) could provide a further CA$45 million in refundable tax credits. Together, these government incentives represent CA$456 million in potential tax credits and tax savings for the Project.

In September 2026, the Government of Canada introduced the proposed Productivity Mega Deduction, allowing immediate deductions for eligible capital investments and Canadian development expenditures. This measure provides an additional potential benefit beyond the incentives identified in the 2025 Feasibility Study, increasing the Project's after-tax NPV by approximately CA$44 million, as reflected in the Updated Feasibility Study's economic analysis. As Québec has yet to confirm implementation of a harmonized measure, any potential additional tax benefits have not been included in the Updated Feasibility Study's after-tax economic analysis. The provincial harmonization could represent a potential NPV benefit of approximately CA$32 million. Together, these measures reinforce the Project's economic competitiveness and the benefits of developing critical minerals in Québec, subject to applicable eligibility requirements and final legislative provisions.

The Project's potential tax credits, deductions, and government support are contingent on eligibility requirements and government approval. There is no guarantee the Company will obtain any or all of the above-mentioned government initiatives.
Next Steps

With the Updated FS now completed, the Company will formally introduce the key Project modifications to the regulators for inclusion into the Environmental and Social Impact Assessment ("ESIA") process, via the existing feedback mechanisms. The first round of information requests has already been received from the Federal level and the same is expected from the Provincial level by year end. The Company expects that the changes introduced by the Updated FS will be seen as either neutral or positive on the Project's environmental and social impacts, and that the process timelines will not be negatively impacted. On this basis, and subject to securing project approvals and financing, FID remains targeted for late 2027.

In the meantime, the Company will continue to advance detailed engineering. Some further optimisation opportunities (such as modularization, which could cut down construction/installation times for certain elements) will be examined through basic and value engineering steps. Current Project schedule targets DMS commissioning to begin in late 2029, with processing activities quickly ramping up to commercial production at the end of Q1 2030.

The Company continues to target release of a Preliminary Economic Assessment ("PEA") later this quarter exploring an alternative development scenario inclusive of both CV5 and CV13 and on all three commodities present – lithium, caesium, and tantalum.

Concurrently with the main Project's authorisations process, the Company intends to continue to pursue its bulk sample advanced exploration project at CV5, via the development of a 2,300 m exploration ramp to access the mineralized zone at two distinct elevations (210 m depth and 245 m depth) to validate key geological, geotechnical, and hydrogeological assumptions for the Project. Development in the mineralized zone would specifically target the high-grade Nova Zone, and even more specifically well-mineralized lithium-caesium-tantalum intercepts to improve geological understanding. The Company has submitted its application for the bulk sample project and is expecting to receive confirmation before the year end.
Conclusion

The Updated FS sets out a stronger starting position for Shaakichiuwaanaan: higher early production, more immediate access to higher grade ore, a simpler DMS processing flowsheet, and a second revenue stream from tantalum as a valuable co-product. By prioritising the high-grade Nova Zone, the underground-first strategy is designed to deliver more spodumene concentrate from fewer tonnes processed earlier in the mine plan, strengthening early cash flow generation while preserving the Project's long-term scale.

Just as importantly, the revised development sequence removes seasonally sensitive activities from the Phase 1 critical path. With no anticipated change to the ESIA authorisations timeline, the Updated FS combines improved economics with a more robust execution pathway, providing a stronger basis for the Company's targeted FID in late 2027.

The Company's focus now turns to advancing detailed engineering, progressing the underground bulk sample program, and developing the commercial and financing framework to support funding of Phase 1. No FID has yet been made; that decision will take into account detailed engineering, prevailing market conditions, available sources of funding, commercial relationships, and customer requirements.

Beyond this development case, the forthcoming PEA will evaluate the potential of an alternative development scenario that integrates both the CV5 and CV13 Pegmatites, extracting value beyond lithium and tantalum, with the addition of caesium. Building on the Updated FS, the PEA expected to be released before year-end will explore the broader opportunity for Shaakichiuwaanaan to become a large-scale, long-life supplier of critical minerals to global markets.

Total cash operating costs (FOB Quebec ports) and total cash operating costs per tonne (FOB Quebec ports):

Criteria used for classification and confidence in Modifying Factors

The Mineral Reserve Estimate is derived entirely from Indicated Mineral Resources within the CV5 Pegmatite. No Measured Mineral Resources have been defined, and no Inferred Mineral Resources have been converted to Mineral Reserves. Inferred Mineral Resources contained within mine designs were treated as waste with zero grade. Following application of mining, metallurgical, economic, environmental, infrastructure, permitting and other Modifying Factors at feasibility study level, the Competent Person determined that the appropriate classification is Probable Mineral Reserve. The resulting Mineral Reserve is 83.0 Mt at 1.27% Li₂O and 148 ppm Ta₂O₅.
Mining methods and mining assumptions

Mining comprises a combination of underground and open-pit extraction. Underground mining uses mechanised long-hole open stoping with cemented paste backfill and is accessed via a single ramp. Underground stopes apply a 95% mining recovery factor with average external dilution of 16.7% (including backfill dilution, ELOS dilution and internal dilution). A minimum underground mining width of 5 m has been applied. Open pit mining is conventional truck-and-shovel mining. Mining dilution for open pit averages 7.6% with 4.1% ore loss and a mining recovery factor of 98%. Underground Mineral Reserves total 34.9 Mt and open pit Mineral Reserves total 48.2 Mt.
Processing method and processing assumptions

Processing is based on conventional crushing and Dense Media Separation (DMS) technology using two processing trains. The process is designed to produce spodumene concentrate grading 5.5% Li₂O and a tantalite concentrate grading 20% Ta₂O₅. Lithium recovery is based on extensive metallurgical testwork undertaken by SGS Canada and varies according to feed grade, averaging approximately 69.7% over life of mine. Average tantalum recovery is approximately 44.6% over life of mine. Iron is controlled through magnetic separation to produce concentrate specifications targeting less than 2.0% Fe₂O₃. No material deleterious elements requiring economic penalties have been identified in the concentrate products.
Basis of cut-off grades

Reserve cut-off grades were determined using feasibility-level operating, processing, transport, royalty and recovery assumptions. The open pit Mineral Reserve cut-off grade is 0.40% Li₂O and the underground Mineral Reserve cut-off grade is 0.70% Li₂O. Cut-off calculations incorporated mining dilution, mining recovery, metallurgical recovery, transport costs and royalties. For conservatism, no revenue was attributed to tantalum when calculating cut-off grades.
Estimation methodology

The Mineral Reserve estimate was completed by BBA Consultants and is based on the July 2026 Mineral Resource Estimate. Mine designs, schedules and economic optimisation were completed to feasibility study level. Open-pit reserves were derived from detailed pit optimisation and mine design. Underground reserves were derived using Deswik Stope Optimiser and detailed mine design supported by geotechnical parameters, dilution estimates, mining recovery factors and economic assessment. Zone-by-zone economic evaluation was undertaken for underground stopes to confirm economic viability.
Material Modifying Factors

Environmental and social baseline studies and an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) have been completed and submitted to federal and provincial regulators. The federal ESIA was deemed complete by the Impact Assessment Agency of Canada in April 2026 and the permitting process is ongoing. The Project is located on mining claims held by the Company within Québec, Canada. No material tenure issues have been identified. Infrastructure assumptions include connection to Hydro-Québec's power network via a proposed 120 kV transmission line, year-round access via the Trans-Taiga Road, concentrate haulage by road to Matagami and onward rail transport to Québec port facilities. Transport, water management, waste management, tailings storage and closure requirements have been incorporated into the feasibility study design and economic evaluation. The Company continues engagement with Eeyou/Cree Nations and an Impact Benefit Agreement is expected prior to operations. No material legal, environmental, permitting or governmental impediments have been identified that would prevent development of the Project, although final approvals remain outstanding.

The Property is situated on Category III Land within the Eeyou Istchee James Bay Territory (Cree Nation of Chisasibi, and Cree Nation of Mistissini), as defined under the James Bay and Northern Québec Agreement ("JBNQA"). Camp Shaakichiuwaanaan is located within the Property's most northern claim block (KCG), to the south side of KM-270 of the Trans-Taiga Road. The camp was constructed by the Company to support ongoing exploration and development activities at the Property, with operations beginning in January 2024. The camp has a current capacity of 88 people, with an expansion of up to 150 people planned.

Radisson, with a population of ~470 people, is the closest community accessible by road from Shaakichiuwaanaan Camp and is located approximately 220 km west of the Property and 245 km west of the Shaakichiuwaanaan Camp.
Radisson is serviced regularly by scheduled flights through the adjacent LG-2 Airport and is the closest airport to the Property with regularly scheduled flights.

The Eeyou/Cree communities of Wemindji and Chisasibi are each located approximately 325 km west of the Property. Both Wemindji and Chisasibi host a larger array of service providers to the region and are serviced by regularly scheduled flights.

Radisson, Wemindji, and Chisasibi, as well as Mirage, are accessible by road with connections to the main provincial network. Therefore, any supplies not available from these locations may be obtained by road from Val-d'Or. Val-d'Or, and the entire Abitibi region, has a long active mining history with significant labour experience to support the Project.

In addition to access by road from nearby communities, charter aircraft may be used to access the La Grande-3 (KM-100) and La Grande-4 (KM-292) airstrips located along the Trans-Taiga Road. Spodumene prices are expected to remain volatile as supply adjusts to growing demand and fluctuating battery-chain inventories. Benchmark Mineral Intelligence's Q3 2026 forecast supports long-term demand growth, with BESS cell supply expanding faster than installed capacity and heavy-duty and commercial vehicles adding meaningful demand. Near-term deficits and a projected return to deficit from 2035 underscore the need for continued investment and successful project delivery and ramp-up. The Feasibility Study's spodumene price assumption gives greater weight to Benchmark's integrated supply-demand and price forecasts, which assess existing operations, development projects, commissioning and ramp-up schedules, and probability-weighted future supply to evaluate market balances and prices over the Project's production period. The selected price is derived from Benchmark's Q3 2026 annual base-case SC6 price forecasts (real), averaged over the 2030 to 2036 period, which yields approximately US$1,950/t for 6% Li₂O spodumene concentrate before any customer-specific commercial adjustments. This period was selected because it captures both the lower prices associated with forecast market surpluses and the subsequent recovery as the market returns to deficit. A grade adjustment of US$162/t is then applied to reflect the lower lithium oxide content of the Project's targeted 5.5% Li₂O product resulting in a final price of US$1,788/t for 5.5% Li₂O spodumene concentrate FOB Québec ports. The Project will produce up to ~800,000 tpa.

Tantalite concentrate is considered a by-product. OnG's October 2026 study anticipates continued price volatility but positive long-term demand from AI infrastructure, capacitors, semiconductors and aerospace. Prices are forecast to ease towards 2029–2030 as Chinese stockpiling slows and supply expands, then recover as demand exceeds supply. However, the forecast includes Shaakichiuwaanaan but excludes other emerging projects, which could narrow deficits and temper the recovery. The updated review supports a fixed long-term Feasibility Study price of US$120/lb of contained tantalite concentrate. The Project will produce an average of ~635,000 lbs of Ta2O5 annually.
